children: Shares of speciality chemicals manufacturer Prasol Chemicals made a weak debut on the stock exchanges on Wednesday, falling nearly 10 per cent below their IPO price despite the issue receiving 3.3 times subscription during the bidding period.

The stock opened at Rs 610 per share on the NSE, compared with the issue price of Rs 676, marking a 9.8 per cent discount. On the BSE, shares began trading at Rs 611, down 9.6 per cent from the offer price.

The subdued listing was broadly in line with signals from the grey market, where the stock had been trading at a discount to its IPO price ahead of the debut. However, grey market premiums are unofficial and can change rapidly, making them an unreliable measure of the actual listing performance.

Prasol Chemicals’ Rs 500 crore IPO was subscribed 3.30 times during the September 8-10 bidding period. The qualified institutional buyer portion was subscribed 7.22 times, while the non-institutional investor and retail portions received 1.80 times and 1.70 times subscription, respectively.
Fresh Capital To Fund Debt Reduction
The company had set the IPO price band at Rs 643-676 per share and raised nearly Rs 150 crore from anchor investors ahead of the issue.

It allotted 22.19 lakh shares to anchor investors at Rs 676 apiece, with domestic mutual funds accounting for more than 45 per cent of the anchor allocation through eight schemes. Investors in the anchor round included Aditya Birla Sun Life Insurance Company, Tata AIA Life Insurance Company, Tata Mutual Fund, Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund, Edelweiss Mutual Fund and ITI Mutual Fund.
The public issue comprised a fresh issue worth up to Rs 80 crore and an offer for sale of shares worth up to Rs 420 crore by existing shareholders.
Prasol Chemicals plans to use the proceeds from the fresh issue towards repayment or pre-payment of borrowings, working capital requirements and general corporate purposes.
Incorporated in 1992, Prasol Chemicals is a forward-integrated manufacturer of acetone-based, phosphorus-based and other speciality chemicals involving complex chemistries.

Its products find applications across pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals and consumer products. Its portfolio includes derivatives used in products such as sunscreens, shampoos, flavours, fragrances and disinfectants.
The company’s business has evolved from its original incorporation as Prachi Poly Products Pvt Ltd. It was renamed Prasol Chemicals in 2007 and subsequently converted into a public company in 2022.

The weak debut comes despite the IPO attracting sufficient demand to close above full subscription, with institutional investors accounting for the strongest participation. The stock’s opening price nevertheless indicates that subscription levels did not translate into a premium at listing.
